title.narrative: Female Economic Empowerment Program (FEEP) in Mozambique

description.narrative: The Female Economic Empowerment Program (FEEP) is an initiative of the Netherlands embassy in Maputo, Mozambique to improve the economic position of women entrepreneurs and female-led micro and small businesses (MSME) in Mozambique. The focus areas of this programme are Beira, Cabo Delgado and Maputo (but other regions in the country are not excluded).The programme aims to enable female entrepreneurs to grow their business through capacity-building and network access and dynamisation of their businesses. Both components will also lead to market and financing opportunities access, through the proposed activities. In the long run, these strengthened female economic actors will contribute to the country's social and economic development and poverty reduction.In order to help strengthen the enabling environment for the entrepreneurial ecosystem in the country, in particular for female entrepreneurship, the project also contributes to capacity building to key bodies of the government of Mozambique; in line with the Mozambique's National Women Economic Empowerment Program (WEEP).

comment.narrative:
Component 3 : CONECTA The FEEP project improved the economic position of women entrepreneurs; female-led micro and small businesses (MSME) in Mozambique; and enable them to grow their business through capacity-building for further access to markets or access to finance.
CONECTA Train of Trainers (ToT) focuses on the enbaling environment for business development of female enmtrepreneurs. Conecta was designed to enhance Mozambique's entrepreneurial ecosystem, with a special focus on supporting female entrepreneurs. It aimed to improve collaboration, clarify roles, and boost communication among ecosystem participants. The program covered topics such as the entrepreneurial ecosystem, challenges, solutions, and effective support strategies. It involved government entities, entrepreneurs, support organizations, and stakeholders to create a more cohesive and informed ecosystem.
Through this ToT the project enhanced the overall entrepreneurial ecosystem, particularly for women, through capacity building of key government bodies in Mozambique involved in entrepreneurship and youth development. This effort was aligned with the National Women Economic Empowerment Program (WEEP) in the country. The State Youth and Employment Secretariat (SEJE) was key partner. The training was aligned with SEJES's multi-year employment and self-employment programs for youth country-wide, to contribute urgently to income and job creation for the youth entering their active age and thus labour market.
The ToT targeted public officers from key government bodies working on youth entrepreneurship were trained to have a better understanding of entrepreneurship,
35 government officials completed intensive Training of Trainers on ideiaLab’s methodology for entrepreneurship and ecosystem approach (19 in person and 16 digital).
